chapter: Cass Carr, Crawley, Burnet and Cootie Williams
title: Cootie's veterans and youngsters, and how long at the Grand Terrace
summary: He lists the older men (Walton, Walker, Perry, Sandy Williams, Bacon) and young wild ones, plus Kenon and Ballard, noting the band recorded in Chicago in April 1942.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Oh, we had a ball. Cootie's band, boy... I mean, he had some band, because it was made up of what Cootie considered... Half of it was veterans, ones that had been in the business a long time, had a little age creepin' up on them, like me... I think I was about 26 then; I had passed the 25-year mark. [IF THIS IS 1942, HE WOULD HAVE BEEN 31

OR 32] And there was men in the band like Greely Walton; there was Jonas Walker, trombone; there was E.V. Perry on first trumpet; and Sandy Williams from the Fletcher Henderson, trombone. These are just the veterans I'm naming.
Was Louis Bacon with you, too.
Yeah, there was Louis Bacon, trumpet. He was from Russell's band, too! Also Chick Webb's band he was from. And he was also the vocalist in Cootie's band. He had a wonderful bass voice. Wonderful.

Then on the younger side, we had men like...I think it was Kenny Kersey; and Milton Fletcher on trumpet; and Joe Guy; Eddie Vinson... Well, Bob Dorsey, I would put him with the younger boys, because he was a nut. He was a real nut. In fact, all of the young ones, they were nuts. Believe me. They didn't care about anything. But they could play.

Oh, Kenny Kersey wasn't there. Or was he? Yeah, I guess Kenny Kersey did open the band. I really don't know who opened... Yeah, he opened up the band. Yeah, I think Kenny Kersey did open the band, because (?)Rich Carter(?) came along later, when we went into the Savoy... Bud Powell. Bud Powell came along later. But anyway, Ken Kersey was all right. He didn't bother nobody.
But them younger ones, Joe Guy and...
You had Norman Kenon on string bass?
Norman Kenon on string bass, yeah. He later went with Basie's band.
The drummer George Ballard?
George Ballard. He was a drummer from Philadelphia, a young boy -- and he went with Duke's band.
Of course, the veteran was Robert Horton.
Robert Horton. Yeah, he was a real veteran. He was older than me. And I was a few years younger than (?).
But that was the nucleus of the band. And they played good music, but everything was a jump. I mean, Cootie wanted to swing, and that's what he had, a Swing band.
Well, it must have been successful if you stayed there so long.
How long?
I mean, because I've got...
You mean at this place.
Yeah, at the Grand Terrace.
How long was I at the Grand Terrace.
Well, I don't know. I just know that in April of '42, you made some recordings in Chicago with that band.
Yeah.
Now, was it the winter of '41 or the winter of '42?
